world.title: Kidney transplantation in older adults - The BMJ
world.summary: Survival benefit depends on the organ offered For people with kidney failure who are suitable for transplantation, the central question is rarely whether transplantation is beneficial in the abstract. It is whether accepting a particular kidney now is likely to offer a survival benefit, as well as improved quality of life, compared with continuing dialysis while waiting for another offer. This decision has become increasingly difficult as transplant programmes consider older and more medically complex candidates and use more kidneys from older donors or after circulatory death.12 A linked study (doi:10.1136/bmj-2026-100624) aims to reduce this uncertainty by using registry data from 64 035 waitlisted dialysis patients across five European registries.3 The authors emulated 60 sequential monthly trials, comparing transplantation during a given month with remaining waitlisted on dialysis during that month.

epidemiology.title: New brief highlights gaps and recommendations for improving violence data on women - World Health Organization (WHO)
epidemiology.summary: A new technical brief calls for more consistent and rigorous measurement of non-partner sexual violence against women and girls – a widespread form of violence that remains underreported and inadequately measured.Non-partner sexual violence, defined as sexual violence perpetrated by someone other than an intimate partner – is a global public health and human rights issue with serious consequences for women’s physical, mental, sexual and reproductive health. An estimated 263 million women and girls aged 15 years and older, or 8% globally, have been subjected to sexual violence from a man other than an intimate partner at least once since the age of 15 years. The prevalence is likely to be much higher because of gaps in available evidence, measurement challenges and the underreporting associated with stigma and fear of repercussions.The new brief by the UNDP/UNFPA/UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development and Research Training in Human Reproduction (HRP), the World Health Organization (WHO) and United Nations partners, identifies key measurement challenges and provides recommendations to researchers, statistical offices and others designing population-based surveys for strengthening the measurement of non-partner sexual violence.Where are the gaps?WHO’s review of population-based surveys, conducted between 2000 and 2023, identified 140 countries with at least one eligible survey, covering 89% of the global population of women and girls aged 15 years and older.

clinical_trials.title: Gut Viruses May Warn of Deadly Intestinal Disease in Preemies Up to Eight Days Early - trialsitenews.com
clinical_trials.summary: Kailun Zhang, PhD, of Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, and colleagues report in Gut that microbial signatures in premature infants may predict necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) up to eight days before symptoms. Analyzing 1,825 longitudinal stool samples from 43 infants who developed NEC and 86 gestational-age- and birthweight-matched controls, researchers found that phage-bacterial signatures predicted early-onset NEC with 75% accuracy and 81% sensitivity, while bacterial antibiotic-resistance profiles predicted late-onset NEC with 83% accuracy.

clinical_trials.title: Mindfulness and Tai Chi Ease Fatigue and Pain After Cancer—but Benefits Are Modest - trialsitenews.com
clinical_trials.summary: Yan Ma, PhD, of the Osher Center for Integrative Health at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women’s Hospital, with lead investigator Linda Carlson, PhD, University of Calgary, and colleagues report in the Journal of Clinical Oncology that mindfulness-based cancer recovery (MBCR) and Tai Chi/Qigong (TCQ) reduced fatigue and pain interference among distressed cancer survivors. In the 587-person MATCH trial, TCQ also improved sleep quality. The findings support mind-body therapies as potentially useful supportive care—but they did not substantially reduce pain intensity, an important distinction between feeling less pain and functioning better despite it.

clinical_trials.title: Boston Children’s Maps New Pathways Behind Dangerous Heart Scarring in HLHS—but ‘Breakthrough’ Needs Perspective - trialsitenews.com

daily_top5.title: WHO launches new primary health care course to strengthen health systems globally - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Health is a human right – yet not everyone can access the health services they need, when and where they need them, without financial hardship. Primary health care (PHC) provides a whole-of-society approach to achieving universal health coverage, putting people and communities at the centre of health systems. Despite nearly 50 years of global commitment to PHC, implementation remains fragmented.
